title: Topic 6 · The Journey Is All There Is · Chunks
source: Modern Wisdom · Chris Williamson & Naval Ravikant · youtu.be/KyfUysrNaco

items.c: the journey is not only the reward
items.s: And the journey is not only the reward, the journey is the only thing there is.
Even success, it’s human nature to bank it very quickly, right,

items.c: the normal loop that we run through
items.s: because the normal loop that we run through is you sit around, you’re bored, then you want something,
because the normal loop that we run through is you sit around, you’re bored, then you want something,
then you start your bout of suffering or anticipation while you strive to get that thing.
If you get that thing then you get used to it, and then you get bored again,
then a few months later you want something else, and if you don’t get it then you’re unhappy for a bit, and then you get over it then you want something else.
That’s the normal cycle. So whether you’re happy or unhappy at the end, it tends not to last.

items.c: there's no point in making money
items.s: Now I don’t wanna be glib and say that there’s no point in making money or being successful.

items.c: Money solves all your money problems
items.zh: 钱能解决你所有跟钱有关的问题
items.s: There absolutely is—money solves all your money problems, so it is good to have money.
That said, there are those stories, I don’t know if you’ve seen those studies, I don’t know how real these are, a lot of these psych studies don’t replicate,

items.zh: 回到他们原本的幸福水平
items.s: but it’s a fun little study that shows that people who break their back and people who win the lottery are back to their baseline happiness two years later.
because then along the way you have both pride and confidence in yourself, and you have a sense of accomplishment,

items.c: you set out to do something
items.s: and you set out to do something and you were right, so I’ll bet that lingers, and then as I said, it solves your money problems.

items.c: you have to enjoy the journey
items.s: So I don’t want to be too glib about it, but I would say in general, this loop that we run through of desire, dopamine, fulfillment, unfulfillment—you have to enjoy the journey.
